_comment: The Infuser: a hempcrete tub built around a cauldron, which is what its recipe says it is (8
hempcrete round a vanilla Cauldron). So the block is hempcrete on the outside and cauldron on the
inside, and it is shaped rather than a cube with a picture of a tub painted on it:
y 0..3    plinth   full 16x16 -- it sits flat on whatever is heating it
y 3..13   waist    inset 1px all round, two iron hoops, the spout bolted through the front
y 13..16  rim      full 16x16 again, so it overhangs the waist and casts a shadow line
x/z 3..13 the pot  an open iron well 12px deep; block/infuser_milk fills it when FILLED
No face carries an explicit `uv` except the spout's. Every other texture here is drawn as a full
16x16 block face and Minecraft's default per-face UV cuts the right piece out of it at the right
coordinates -- the same trick vanilla's cauldron uses, and the reason textures-src/infuser.mctex
is banded by row. The spout is the exception because it pokes out past z=0, and a negative
coordinate has no sensible default UV; its faces index regions of block/infuser_spout that the
mctex spells out.
ambientocclusion is off for the same reason vanilla's cauldron turns it off: AO on an open-topped
box smears a false shadow across the inner walls. The block must also be nonOpaque() in ModBlocks
or neighbours cull their faces against the inset waist and you can see through the gap.

elements._comment: plinth. Its up face is only ever seen as the 1px ledge the inset waist leaves.
waist, north wall. Outside is the spout face; inside is the pot.
the bottom of the pot, one quad. Sits a pixel above the plinth so the two never fight.
rim, four pieces. Full width, so it overhangs the waist by a pixel on every side.

_comment: the spout's arm, plumbed through the front wall and out 2px past the block. It is geometry
and not paint because a player has to read 'a finished batch comes out here, into whatever
is against this face' off the block alone -- no vanilla processing block pushes its own
output, so nothing else in the game teaches that rule.

elements._comment: the nozzle it drips from. Runs back to z=1 so it lands flush on the waist wall.
